newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ short end gives up some of its gains at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ short end gives up some of its gains at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 93.15 (PREV 93.13) 90-DAYS 6.88 (PREV 6.92)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.50 PCT (PREV 6.50) US 5-YR 6.28 (PREV 6.31)
NZ MCI -0.94 (PREV -0.91)
New Zealand debt surrendered some of its early gains during Thursday's session but still managed to end stronger across the curve.
Dealers expect the market to remain in a narrow range with yield upside limited.

The monetary conditions index eased to 94 basis points looser than the Reserve Bank's March desired level but that has merited little market discussion with traders arguing that the bank previously failed to express concern when the index rose over 100.
"The market is holding in well considering the MCI is close to 100," said one senior bond trader.
A bullish Australian market was supportive of the local scene.
The bill futures had risen in the morning to a high of 93.23 but dealers said the market had been pushed artificially high at the time of a couple of rate sets. The contract closed up two at 93.15.
The 02/01 maturity ended one basis point stronger at 6.82 percent, while the long bond was four stronger at 7.02 percent.
The bond market is less concerned about global factors now and is starting to seriously focus on next Thursday's budget and the Monetary Policy Statement the next day, dealers said.
The main interest in the budget will be the size of the bond tender programme.

Comments by Treasurer Winston Peters today that the 1997/98 operating surplus may be lower than forecast because of a couple of one-off items may have tilted traders to the view that the programme will be at the upper end of the $500 million to $1.5 billion range.
However, that is not necessarily seen as bad for bonds as lack of liquidity could be a negative for the market.

Building consents data this morning showed the economy had not hit the wall as hard as some imagined and dealers said new dwelling estimates data on Friday morning will be closely watched to see if the April building figures were a rogue figure.
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
